title: Suppliers, customers, landlords and employers
course_title: Negotiation Skills for Business and Life

say: Suppliers, customers, landlords and employers.
This is the video for Module 3 of Negotiation Skills for Business and Life.
Every naira you save when buying, and every naira you protect when selling, goes straight to your profit. These are long-term relationships, so aim for deals the other side is happy to repeat.

panel.heading: The negotiations you meet most
items: Rent and pay: balance the power

say: Landlords and employers have more formal power than you. Good preparation, respect and objective evidence help balance that power.

panel.heading: The negotiations you meet most
items: Rent and pay: balance the power

say: A low unit price can hide costs. Always compare suppliers on landed cost. That is the price per unit plus delivery, packaging and losses from damaged goods.
Supplier A charges 1900 a yard, all upfront, plus 8000 delivery. Landed cost, 388000 naira.
Supplier B charges 1950, with free delivery, and half now, half after delivery. Landed cost, 390000. Only 2000 more, and paying half later helps her cash flow.
So Rukayat asks B. If I order 300 yards for the next two terms, can you do a better price on the same terms? B offers 1900.
Now she gets A's price with B's better terms, paying 285000 now and the rest after delivery.
Customers often ask, what is the last price? That is normal and friendly. Plan for it.
If a dress costs you 9000 to make and you sell at 15000, a 3000 discount cuts your profit in half, from 6000 to 3000.

Take a deposit for custom work

say: So offer value instead. Free delivery in your area, a small extra item, or faster finishing.

say: Use quantity breaks, for example 15000 each, or 42000 for three.

say: For custom work, many tailors, caterers and bakers ask a deposit of 50% to 70% before buying materials.

say: With landlords, gather evidence first. Ask three other tenants in the area what they pay, and note leaks or broken things.

panel.heading: Before you pay any rent
items: Ask three tenants nearby what they pay
Inspect in person, speak to the landlord

say: More than the amount can be discussed. Ask to pay in two instalments, and agree who fixes what before you pay.

panel.heading: Before you pay any rent
items: Ask three tenants nearby what they pay
Inspect in person, speak to the landlord

say: Ask for receipts for every fee, and whether the caution deposit is refundable.

panel.heading: Before you pay any rent
items: Ask three tenants nearby what they pay
Inspect in person, speak to the landlord

say: Inspect the property in person, and speak to the landlord directly. Pay into an account in the landlord's or agency's name.

panel.heading: Before you pay any rent

say: Fake agents collect money for places they do not own. If a demand seems unusual, ask a lawyer, a tenants' association or a trusted community leader before you pay.

panel.rule: Never pay before you inspect and confirm the real owner

say: You may keep your walk-away point private. That is acceptable.
But never state things you know are false. Trust, once lost, costs far more than one deal. In a community where people talk, your reputation for fair dealing is one of your strongest assets.
To remember. Compare suppliers on landed cost. Give value before you cut price. Never pay rent before you inspect and verify the owner.
Bring evidence to a pay talk. And keep your limit private, but never state false facts. Confirm every agreement in writing.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Offer value and quantity breaks, not cuts
Inspect and verify before paying rent
Keep your limit private, never lie
